alana: Quick check — onboarding lambda-13b checkpoint. I see the safetensors bundle at s3://redwood-models/lambda13b/v1/weights/ but the shard index (index.json / shard TTL metadata) looks missing from the upload. Also noticed tokenizer vocab has a weird \u0120 mapping for unk. Anyone seen this before or should I re-run the packer?

mike: @alana I pulled the bucket earlier. There are weight shards but no index.json. devops-bot might have logs for the upload job. Did the uploader exit nonzero?

devops-bot: upload-job-38765 finished: SUCCESS. Uploaded 64 objects to s3://redwood-models/lambda13b/v1/weights/. Metadata keys: Content-Length, ETag, x-amz-meta-shard (present). No index.json created by job 38765.

sara: Two quick possibilities: 1) the packer ran in `--shard --upload` mode and expects a separate index step; 2) the index writer failed due to a transient permissions error. Can you share `ls -la` and we can confirm filenames?

alana: here's a snippet I ran from a machine with creds: ```
$ aws s3 ls s3://redwood-models/lambda13b/v1/weights/ --human-readable
2026-03-15 09:01:22   1.8 GiB  shard-00000-of-00064.safetensors
2026-03-15 09:01:22   1.8 GiB  shard-00001-of-00064.safetensors
...
2026-03-15 09:01:24   1.6 GiB  tokenizer.json
2026-03-15 09:01:24     12 KiB  merges.txt
```

jay: Re: tokenizer oddity — which tokenizer format is it (hf/tokenizers json or sentencepiece)? If tokenizer.json exists, run this quick check to print special tokens: ```python
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
t = Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer.json')
print(t.get_vocab()['<unk>'])
print(t.token_to_id('[BOS]'))
``` If <unk> maps to a nonzero id and the model expects id 0 for unk, we'll get off-by-one outputs. Seen this cause garbled prompts.

alana: it's huggingface tokenizer.json (not spm). When I introspected locally, <unk> id = 5 and model's config.json has "unk_token_id": 0 — mismatch. That explains some of the quick smoke failures (weird logits for first token).

esther: For the index.json / shard TTL: our packer has a two-step flow: `packer --shard --upload` then `packer --write-index`. If upload completes but the index step fails, we leave shards without index.json. We should either make the packer atomic or add a reconciler job. Short-term: run `packer --write-index --bucket s3://redwood-models/lambda13b/v1/weights/ --shard-count 64` then validate.

mike: +1 to run the write-index. Also note the TP layout in the model config: "tensor_parallel": 8 and shard naming is interleaved (shard-00000-of-00064 ...). The packer needs the same TP flag or index offsets will be wrong for KV cache ordering.

alana: question for @jay / @sara — when writing index, do we need to supply `--tp-layout interleave`? Current packer default is contiguous. If we write index with contiguous when model expects interleaved, serve will map ranks incorrectly.

jay: Yes, pass `--tp-layout interleave` for this model. The model's saved weights were created with TP=8 interleaved (I checked the original exporter note). If you can't re-run exporter, the index writer can reorder pointers but you must set `--tp-layout interleave` explicitly.

esther: conversion command I'd use: ```bash
packer convert --input ./exported_weights/ --format safetensors --dtype fp16 --shard-count 64 --tp-layout interleave --output ./pack_output/ && 
packer upload --path ./pack_output/ --bucket s3://redwood-models/lambda13b/v1/weights/ && 
packer write-index --bucket s3://redwood-models/lambda13b/v1/weights/ --shard-count 64 --tp-layout interleave
``` Add `--force` if you want to overwrite.

mike: Also be careful about fp16 vs bf16. The exporter used bf16 for some attention kernels; we want consistent dtype. If model.cfg says dtype bf16 but we upload fp16 shards, runtime may downcast unexpectedly. Check model config: ```json
{"dtype":"bf16","tensor_parallel":8}
```

alana: ok I'll do these steps: 1) patch tokenizer mapping to set unk_token_id to 5 in config (or adjust model's expected id), 2) re-run write-index with `--tp-layout interleave`, 3) checksum shard order and validate KV ordering. I'll push a small helper script and a PR.

mike: For checksum, this helped me before: ```bash
aws s3api list-objects --bucket redwood-models --prefix lambda13b/v1/weights/ --query 'Contents[?contains(Key, "shard-")].{Key:Key,ETag:ETag}' > /tmp/shard_etags.json
python scripts/verify_shard_order.py /tmp/shard_etags.json --expected-count 64
```

devops-bot: reconciler-job-842 queued to run index sweep on 2026-03-15T10:00:00Z. Will attempt to create missing index.json if packer metadata present.

alana: filed PR #4126 with the small `tokenizer_patch.py` and updated packer flags. Ping @sara and @jay for quick review? :rocket: :eyes:

sara: Reviewing now. Quick note — please include a short deterministic test that loads the tokenizer and asserts unk_token_id matches model config. Saves a retry cycle.

jay: LGTM pending test. If reconciler job creates index before you write, the packer write-index will no-op safely if `--force` not set.

alana: thanks all — will follow up after PR lands and after reconciler run.
